summary: Slovakia is an EU and Schengen member: EU/EEA citizens need no visa, some 60 visa-waiver nationalities — including the US, UK, Japan and most of the Americas — get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and other travelers need a Schengen visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs may be rare in mountain areas and small villages.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says there is a risk of petty crime, especially in Bratislava, where pickpockets operate around the main tourist areas, the Christmas markets and bars. For hikers it advises staying on marked trails and checking local warnings before setting out, because bear sightings and occasional attacks have been reported.

The UK government says that if you need the Slovak Mountain Rescue Service (HZS) you will have to meet costs of up to €1,000, advises making sure your insurance includes rescue costs, and says ignoring HZS rules or instructions can bring a fine of up to €3,320.
Visa-waiver nationals will need an ETIAS travel authorization once the EU system becomes mandatory; the EU says it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Slovakia?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens need no visa. Citizens of some 60 visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas — get 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area. Everyone else needs a Schengen visa from a Slovak embassy or visa center.

faq.question: Is Slovakia in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says Slovakia follows Schengen area rules, and the 90/180-day visa-free allowance is counted across the entire area, not per country.

faq.question: Will I need ETIAS for Slovakia?
faq.answer: Once the EU's ETIAS system becomes mandatory, visa-waiver travelers will need the online authorization before their trip. The EU says it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s), be valid for three years or until the passport expires, and that it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: What currency does Slovakia use?
faq.answer: The euro, according to Canada's travel advice.
